blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Rubric hacking limits both performance and training robustness in rubric-based reinforcement learning. By decomposing rubrics into sub-dimensions, we reveal the Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence: as the total rubric score increases, certain sub-dimension scores systematically decrease, suggesting the model sacrifices specific quality aspects to optimize the aggregated objective. From the sub-dimension perspective, we observe two phenomena: (1) dimension imbalance, causing the policy to favor heavily covered dimensions; (2) dimension absence, leading to a systematic gap between rewards and true quality. To mitigate these issues, we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA), which has generations compete within each dimension separately to mitigate rubric imbalance, and Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC), which mines evaluation dimensions implicitly encoded in a holistic preference signal to complete rubric coverage. Experiments in chat, science, and medical domains indicate that FRDA mitigates rubric hacking with more stable improvements, while RSDC outperforms both single-reward training and naive multi-reward aggregation, yielding generally higher-quality responses.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Rubric Dimension Decomposition. Rubric-based reinforcement learning ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Viswanathan et al., 2025 ; Tyagi et al., 2026 ) extends the verifiable reward reinforcement learning (RLVR) paradigm ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Yu et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025 ; Aggarwal and Welleck, 2025 ; Qian et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026a ) to open-ended tasks with fine-grained, interpretable signals, but rubric hacking remains a key bottleneck limiting its performance and stability. As shown in Figure 1 , rubric hacking ( Mahmoud et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) typically manifests as a continuous increase in overall rubric reward during training, while generation quality declines after an initial improvement. Existing work ( Yang et al., 2026 ) mitigates this by reducing overfitting to the judge model’s biased criteria, without analyzing how the internal composition of the overall rubric reward changes. To investigate this, we track how reward shifts within the rubric during training. Since prompts vary in criteria count and criteria are overly specific and semantically fragmented, criterion-level analysis is difficult. We therefore decompose rubrics into semantic dimensions per task domain, each abstract, relatively independent, and covering a major aspect of generation quality.

blocks.en: Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence. Taking the chat task as an example, we divide rubric criteria into five explicit semantic dimensions: instruction following, factual reliability, reasoning helpfulness, communication style, and safety boundary. As shown in Figure 2 (a), the overall rubric reward keeps rising while the communication style dimension stagnates. To rule out semantic overlap inevitably introduced by manual partitioning, we apply Cholesky residual whitening ( Kessy et al., 2018 ) to decorrelate the explicit semantic dimensions, yielding whitened latent dimensions that each retain only the reward information unique to that dimension. As shown in Figure 2 (b), the latent dimensions of factual reliability and communication style exhibit a clear downward trend. Guided by the communication style latent dimension, we trace back training samples and find that its decline corresponds to the model ignoring finer-grained requirements such as readability and conciseness, instead inflating rubric hit rates by enumerating irrelevant or redundant content—a behavior that runs counter to true generation quality. We further explicitly extract conciseness-related criteria: as shown in Figure 2 (c), their scores also decline steadily, and as shown in Figure 2 (d), they account for 33.37% of the communication style dimension’s weight, closely matching the latent dimension’s trend. This cross-validation shows that the pattern is not random fluctuation; rather, as the overall rubric reward rises, the model systematically sacrifices certain sub-dimensions, a phenomenon we term Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence .
blocks.zh: 鲁布里克内部奖励差异. 以聊天任务为例,我们把标题标准分为五个明确的语义维度:以下指令,事实可靠性,推理帮助,通信风格,和安全界限. 如图2(a)所显示,总的奖赏在传播风格方面停滞不前的同时不断上升。 为了排除人工分解不可避免地引入的语义重叠,我们采用Cholesky剩余白化(Kessy等,2018年)来装饰明显的语义维度,产生白化的潜在维度,每个维度只保留该维度独有的奖励信息. 如图2(b)所示,事实可靠性和沟通方式的潜在层面呈现出明显的下降趋势。 在交流风格潜在维度的指引下,我们追溯到培训样本,发现其下降符合模型忽略了精细的刻度要求,如可读性和简洁性,而是通过列举无关或多余的内容来夸大标分打击率——这种行为违背了真正的生成质量。 我们进一步明确提出与简洁性有关的标准:如图2(c)所示,它们的分数也稳步下降,如图2(d)所示,它们占通信风格维度的33.37%,与潜在的维度趋势密切相匹配。 这种交叉验证表明,模式不是随机波动;相反,随着整体的悬赏率上升,模型系统地牺牲了某些分数,我们称之为 " Rubric奖励差异 " 的现象。

blocks.en: Rubric Dimension Imbalance. Motivated by this finding, we analyze the distribution of rubric criteria across semantic dimensions in three training domains and observe a clear imbalance, as shown in Figure 2 (e). In the chat task, in both the original and whitened semantic spaces, upward-trending dimensions carry much larger weights than stagnant or declining ones, indicating that densely covered dimensions dominate reward aggregation and cause the model to sacrifice sparsely covered ones. To mitigate this, inspired by the multi-reward RL algorithm GDPO ( Liu et al., 2026a ) , we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA): first compute rubric sub-dimension group advantages, then aggregate them with equal weights, letting generations compete separately within each dimension. This forces the model to perform well on more dimensions to achieve high reward, weakening the dominance of dense dimensions and reducing sacrifice of sparse dimensions.

Rubric Visific Imball. 基于这一调查结果,我们分析了三个培训领域语义层面的标点标准分布情况,并观察到明显的不平衡,如图2(e)所示。 在聊天任务中,无论是在原始的还是被白化的语义空间中,上调维度比停滞或下降的维度要重得多,表明覆盖度高的维度主导了奖励的集合,并导致模型牺牲被少有被覆盖的维度. 为了缓解这种情况,在多奖RL算法GDPO(Liu等,2026a)的启发下,我们提出"公平率维度聚合"(FRDA):首先计算出"分分分分分"组的优势,再以等分的权重来汇总,让世代在每一维分内分别竞争. 这迫使模型在更多维度上表现良好,以获得高回报,削弱密集维度的主导地位并减少稀有维度的牺牲.

blocks.en: Rubric Dimension Absence. As shown in Figure 2 (f), a single prompt covers only 2–5 semantic dimensions, since annotators cannot cover all evaluation criteria—a fundamental difference from RLVR. A holistic preference signal implicitly encodes a relatively complete human evaluation system. To this end, we propose Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC): leveraging the decorrelation property of Cholesky whitening residuals, it mines from the holistic preference signal semantic dimensions not yet annotated in the rubric, filling the potential coverage gap in rubric criteria.
blocks.zh: 鲁布里克维度缺失。 如图2(f)所显示,单一的提示只涵盖2至5个语义维度,因为注释者无法涵盖所有评价标准——这是与RLVR的根本区别。 整体偏好信号隐含地编码了一个相对完整的人类评价系统. 为此,我们提议剩余语义维度(RSDC):利用Cholesky白化后残留物的装饰属性,从标题中尚未加注的整体偏好信号语义维度来取出地雷,填补了标题标准中潜在的覆盖空白.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are:
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献是:

blocks.en: • We identify intra-rubric reward divergence , a previously underexplored form of rubric hacking in which the aggregate rubric reward increases while specific semantic dimensions systematically decline. • We propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA) , which has generations compete within each dimension separately to mitigate rubric imbalance. • We propose Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC) , the first to implicitly mine complementary quality dimensions from global preferences without explicitly adding rubric criteria. • Extensive experiments on chat, science, and medical tasks show that FRDA effectively mitigates rubric hacking, and RSDC significantly outperforms both single-reward training and naive multi-reward aggregation, offering a new perspective on jointly leveraging interpretable rubric rewards and holistic preference rewards.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Rubric Reinforcement Learning. RaR ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) and Rubric Anchors ( Huang et al., 2025 ) established rubric scores as fine-grained reward signals for reinforcement learning on open-ended tasks, while Checklist Feedback ( Viswanathan et al., 2025 ) uses instruction-specific checklists to provide training rewards. OpenRubric ( Liu et al., 2026b ) and RubricHub scale rubric construction through LLM-based generation. These works directly use the overall rubric score as the training reward. POW3R ( Tyagi et al., 2026 ) reweights criteria according to the variance of judgments within a sampled group, concentrating optimization on criteria with greater discriminative power.
blocks.zh: 鲁布里克强化学习. RaR (Gunjal等,2026年)和Rubric Anchors(Huang等,2025年)将分数确定为在开放式任务上强化学习的精细奖赏信号,而"明细清单反馈"(Viswanathan等,2025年)则使用特定指令清单来提供培训奖励. OpenRubric (Liu等, 2026b.)和RubricHub通过以LLM为主的生成来进行比例尺的构建. 这些作品直接使用总分作为训练奖励. POW3R(Tyagi等,2026年)根据被抽样群体内部的判断差异重新加权标准,以更大的歧视力量集中优化标准.

blocks.en: Rubric Hacking. Mahmoud et al. ( Mahmoud et al., 2026 ) document rubric reward hacking as divergence between the training verifier and a stronger judge, attributing it to verifier failure and rubric limitations; CHERRL ( Wang et al., 2026 ) reproduces this by injecting judge biases and detecting their exploitation. Both are diagnostic, revealing rubric hacking but offering no solutions. The closest work, Rubric Dropout ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , inspired by neural dropout, randomly drops rubric parts so the model cannot rely on any particular criterion to game the rubric. However, existing methods ignore internal dynamics within the rising overall rubric reward. Revealing Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence via rubric dimension-wise decomposition is our core insight; we thus propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA) to mitigate rubric hacking, unlike existing methods. This offers a new perspective; our method is orthogonal to Dropout, and their combination is future work.

(Mahmoud等人, 2026年)文件将黑客作为培训核查员与更强有力的法官之间的分歧给予奖励,将其归结为核查员的失败和名义限制;CHERRL(Wang等人, 2026年)通过向法官注入偏见并发现其利用情况来转载这一点。 两者都是诊断性的,揭示出粗略的黑客化,但没有给出任何解决方案. 最接近的作品"Rubric Droppout"(杨等,2026年)被神经退位所激发出,随机地放下了路由部件,使模型无法依靠任何特定标准来游戏路由. 然而,现有方法忽视了整体回报不断上升的内部动态。 我们的核心见解是通过微分维度分解来揭示Rubric内部的分分辨;因此,我们提议公平-分量相加(FRDA),以减少微分黑客,这与现有方法不同。 这提供了一个新的视角;我们的方法是正统的辍学,两者的结合就是今后的工作。

4.2 Effectiveness of Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation
blocks.zh: 4.2 公平率层面的效用

blocks.en: As shown in Table 1 , on Chat and Science, FRDA improves over raw rubric reward in w-mean by Δ = + 5.05 \Delta=+5.05 on Arena-Hard v2.0, +3.60 on ResearchQA, and +8.99 on GPQA Diamond, exceeding the better Dropout variant on each by +2.92, +1.40, and +4.75 points. On Medical (HealthBench), FRDA still improves over raw rubric reward ( Δ = + 1.92 \Delta=+1.92 ) and performs on par with Dropout. As Figure 2 (e) shows, the Chat and Science training sets have a more imbalanced per-dimension criteria weight distribution than Medical. This is consistent with the results above: where training-time dimension weights are more skewed, computing advantages within each dimension and then aggregating them with equal weights can effectively mitigate dimension imbalance, in line with FRDA’s larger margin over Dropout’s generic overfitting regularization; on the comparatively balanced Medical set, there is less imbalance for FRDA’s structural adjustment to act on, in line with its performance being close to Dropout while still improving over raw rubric reward. These results suggest FRDA and Dropout address rubric hacking from two different, orthogonal angles, one structural and one regularization-based: Dropout provides consistently stable optimization, whereas FRDA is more effective when the training set has imbalanced dimension coverage. Combining the two could be worth exploring in future work.

blocks.en: FRDA Mitigates Rubric Hacking Rather Than Merely Slowing Training. One might attribute FRDA’s gains (Figure 5 , Table 1 ) to slower training, such that the policy has not yet reached the stage of sacrificing sparsely covered dimensions. Figure 6 rules this out: in all three domains, FRDA’s aggregate rubric reward closely tracks that of raw rubric reward at nearly every step, with no delay. Yet FRDA reaches a higher test peak and stays above raw rubric reward over steps 400–600. The gain thus stems not from how fast the reward grows, but from where it is spent: per-dimension competition spreads improvement across dimensions instead of concentrating it in densely covered ones.
blocks.zh: FRDA 减缓鲁布里克·哈克宁而不是仅仅慢化训练。 人们可能会将复兴民主阵线的成果(图5,表1)归咎于培训进度较慢,以致于该政策尚未达到牺牲所覆盖的稀有层面的阶段。 图6排除了这种情况:在所有三个领域,FRDA的汇总奖赏都密切跟踪了几乎每一步的原始奖赏,没有拖延。 然而,FRDA达到了更高的测试峰值,在400-600步的原始奖励之上。 因此,收益不是来自奖励增长的多快,而是来自奖励的花费地点:每次分配竞争将改善扩大到不同层面,而不是将奖励集中在覆盖密集的层面。

Figures 7 (a) and 7 (b) plot each Chat dimension’s Cholesky-whitened residual (Section 3.3 ) for FRDA (solid) vs. raw rubric reward (dashed).
For dimensions trending downward under raw rubric reward, FRDA’s decline is visibly shallower, and for those trending upward, the rise is similarly damped; both curves diverge increasingly from step 400 onward, with FRDA staying closer to its step-400 level.

blocks.en: Ablation: Average Dimension Mean vs. FRDA. A seemingly simpler fix for dimension imbalance is to average the unnormalized dimension-level rewards r d ​ ( x , y ) r_{d}(x,y) with equal weights, replacing the weighted mean in Eq. ( 3 ) with a plain average over covered dimensions; we call this ablation Average Dimension Mean (ADM) and train it on Chat under the same setup as FRDA. Table 3 shows ADM falls below even the raw-rubric-reward baseline ( Δ = − 2.65 \Delta=-2.65 ): equal-weight averaging ignores how differently separated each dimension’s raw score distribution is, so a sparsely covered or noisy dimension with a wide score range dominates the aggregate, merely trading the original imbalance for a new one favoring high-variance dimensions. FRDA avoids this by normalizing each dimension’s advantage to zero mean and unit variance within the sampling group (Eq. ( 4 )) before averaging, so balancing acts on the group-relative advantage rather than the raw reward. Mitigating rubric hacking thus requires balancing at the right statistical level; naive re-weighting can introduce a bias as harmful as the one it removes.
blocks.zh: 偏差:平均尺寸平均值对FRDA. 对维度不平衡的一个看似比较简单的解决办法是,将未正常的维度级别奖励r d (x,y) r_{d} (x,y) 以等分权取而代之,将Eq (3) 的加权平均值取而代之,使其比所覆盖的维度更纯正;我们称之为这种减值平均维度平均值(ADM),并在与FRDA相同的设置下在Chat上进行训练. 表3显示ADM甚至低于原始-rubric-奖励基准(QQ=- 2.65\Delta=-2.65): 等重平均值忽略了每个维度的原始分数分布如何不同,因此一个覆盖范围很广或吵闹的维度主宰了总和,仅仅用原来的不平衡来换一个偏好高变异度的新维度. FRDA避免了这种情况,将每个维度的优势在平均值(Eq. (4 ))之前变成零平均值和单位差异,从而平衡了对群体相对优势而不是原始回报的行为。 因此,减轻轻度黑客行为需要在正确的统计层面实现平衡;天真的再加权可带来与其去掉的一样有害的偏见。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: By decomposing rubric rewards into semantic dimensions, we identify Intra-Rubric Reward Divergence, a form of rubric hacking in which aggregate rubric reward keeps rising while specific sub-dimensions decline, and trace it to two causes: dimension imbalance and dimension absence. To address them, we propose Fair-Race Dimension Aggregation (FRDA), which normalizes and aggregates rubric sub-dimensions with equal weights so generations compete separately within each dimension, mitigating the dominance of densely covered dimensions over the reward signal, and Residual Semantic Dimension Completion (RSDC), which uses Cholesky whitening to extract from a holistic preference signal the latent dimensions not covered by the rubric. Experiments on chat, science, and medical domains show that FRDA effectively mitigates rubric hacking when the rubric training set has imbalanced dimension coverage and performs comparably to Dropout when it is balanced, while RSDC outperforms both single-reward training and naive multi-reward aggregation.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Our analysis relies on a manual, coarse-grained partition of rubric criteria into semantic dimensions per domain, which requires domain-knowledgeable annotators and may vary across annotators; we do not pursue a fine-grained or universally agreed-upon decomposition.
blocks.zh: 我们的分析依赖于人工、粗糙地将标题标准分解成每个域的语义维度,这需要域能知识的注释者,而且可能因注释者而异;我们不追求精细或普遍同意的分解。

blocks.en: Because specialized preference reward models for science and medicine are not readily available off the shelf, we validate RSDC only on chat, where a general-purpose conversational reward model exists; extending it to professional domains is left to future work.
blocks.zh: 由于科学和医学的专业优先奖赏模型不易从架子上取出,我们只在聊天时验证RSDC,在聊天时存在通用的谈话奖赏模型;将其推广到专业领域留待未来工作.
